as_told.title: Tesla's files seized by the FBI and reviewed by John Trump

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after the famous inventor Nikola Tesla died, the FBI seized his files, and John Trump, an MIT professor, the country's leading radar expert and Donald Trump's uncle, was sent to go through them around 1943. According to Michels, the task was to see whether anything in them could help national security or give the US an edge in war. He tells it in several episodes, sometimes dating it loosely to the 1940s, as a sign that the government took Tesla's ideas seriously.
